brief: Goldman Sachs equity sales daily. Mostly a reported roundup, with two argued sections. A 162k jobs print against 55k, plus rising oil and the Fed debate, left the S&P down 38bps at 7718 and moved markets to price a 60% chance of a September Fed hike, with the US 10yr at 4.78% and Brent at $97. Goldman's own view runs the other way: it expects a fully priced 25bps ECB hike Thursday to be the last of the cycle, because H2 growth runs below trend, core pressures build only modestly, energy prices come in under forwards, and the Fed does not hike. Trump threatened to cut trade with surplus countries unless the Fed cuts, saying rates should be 1%, not 4%. Reported items include Samsung guiding 2027 memory supply tighter than 2026, hyperscaler bond issuance heading to $320bn, Anthropic's $517bn of compute contracts, German funded pension assets at 7% of GDP, a Dutch gold relocation out of New York, Tesla's Austin Cybercab launch, and a CLARITY Act floor vote on 15 Sep. Allocation stays tactically neutral for 3m and modestly pro-risk for 12m.
